analysis: The only changed file is CHANGELOG.md, with two new bullets under a new heading at lines 1-9. The first covers the interactive model picker (`darkbloom start`/`switch`): it now cancels when its terminal hangs up, restores the terminal mode, and leaves the provider unchanged. The second covers a provider started by hand (`start --local`, or `start --foreground` in a terminal): a SIGHUP now triggers the same cooperative drain as Ctrl-C and SIGTERM. The launchd-run provider and a start made with SIGHUP ignored (e.g. under nohup) behave as before. This is documentation only, and the source changes are not supplied. I found no change to the authorization, attestation, encryption, billing or data-exposure behaviour that the threat model tracks. The described behaviour touches the provider process lifecycle (TB-003/TB-007 and availability) and the shutdown drain, but the claimed change is graceful drain on SIGHUP, which does not weaken any security control. Coverage limit: the Swift signal-handling and picker implementation was not provided, so I could not verify the drain path, for example that in-flight requests stay properly cancelled or that the terminal-restore logic is correct. The next pass should check the real source for those points if it is available. No new threat-model gap arises from the changelog text alone.
